title: Delivery and installation of a High ion density etcher for lithium niobate on insulator - LiNb03 (LN)
description: DTU Nanolab wishes to acquire a high ion density source reactive ion etcher for etching lithium niobate on insulator 150 mm wafer processing. Delivery is expected no later than Q4 2027. We are looking for a highly versatile instrument providing stable etch recipes, capable of etching at both nanometer scale and micrometer scale with precise control of etching depth, typically a few hundreds of nm. The instrument must have state-of-the-art performance in terms of profile control, uniformity, selectivity, and in particu-lar etching sidewall smoothness to achieve low waveguide loss. The Instrument will be installed in the DTU Nanolab cleanroom - a university facility providing a comprehensive suite of micro- and nanofabrication tools. It serves a diverse community of over 200 active users, ranging from novice students to experienced researchers, as well a high percentage of commercial clients. At DTU Nanolab there are several research groups and companies working on developing and running small scale production of optical devises on the tools. Therefor the capability of etching smooth optical waveguide, gratings and other low-roughness optical devises are of high importance to us.

description: Die Gemeinde Benningen am Neckar und die Stadt Marbach am Neckar haben sich für die gemeinsame Gartenschau beworben und den Zuschlag für die Ausrichtung der Gartenschau 2033 erhalten. Treffpunkte geschaffen und die Verbindung beider Kommunen gestärkt werden. Im Mittelpunkt steht der Neckar als verbindendes Element. Die Daueranlagen sollen dauerhaft in die Siedlungsstruktur eingebunden werden. Kulturelle und historische Orte werden gezielt einbezogen und gestärkt. Die Teilräume der Daueranlagen weisen unterschiedliche Qualitäten auf, die herausgearbeitet und weiterentwickelt werden sollen. Naturnahe Bereiche stehen neben siedlungsnahen und kulturell geprägten Räumen. Neue Zugänge und behutsame Gestaltungen sollen bisher wenig erschlossene Orte erlebbar machen. Es werden eigenständige, innovative und identitätsstiftende Konzepte gesucht, die Entwurfsideen entwickeln, die die Bereiche der Daueranlagen neu interpretieren, überraschende Perspektiven eröffnen und eine starke, wiedererkennbare Haltung formulieren. Insgesamt wird ein zusammenhängendes Konzept erwartet, das eine gemeinsame Identität der Daueranlagen schafft und zugleich die Besonderheiten der einzelnen Orte betont. Aufbauend auf bereits umgesetzten Maßnahmen soll ein langfristig tragfähiges Entwicklungskonzept entstehen, das kurzfristige Impulse setzt und die schrittweise Umsetzung der ISEK-Maßnahmen innerhalb der kommenden zehn Jahre ermöglicht.

Ter vergelijking: dit komt overeen met de gemiddelde CO2 uitstoot van het energieverbruik van 30.816 huishoudens. In 2024 heeft HVC na een aanbestedingsprocedure een contract afgesloten met leverancier SLB Capturi | SLB Capturi (SLBC) voor de bouw van een CO2 afvanginstallatie op HVC-locatie in Alkmaar. Daarnaast omvat de opdracht de aanleg van hemelwater- en terreinriolering, drainagevoorzieningen, groenvoorzieningen en verkeersvoorzieningen. Verder omvat de opdracht het realiseren van funderingen voor de diverse procesinstallaties en gebouwen, waaronder funderingspalen, zware in het werk gestorte betonconstructies, fundatieplaten, kelderconstructies, vloeren, opstortingen en vloeistofkerende verhardingen. description: General. This is a Sources Sought and is for informational/market research purposes only. This is not a Request for Proposals, Quotations, or an Invitation for Bids. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to obtain information regarding the interest, capabilities, capacity, and qualifications of industry so the Government can make informed business decisions. We are seeking responses from both large and small businesses, including Small Businesses, Small Disadvantaged Businesses, 8(a) participants, Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) firms, Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB) concerns, Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) firms, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) concerns and Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) entities. All interested parties are encouraged to respond. Project Background. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Portland District (NWP) is seeking interested and capable sources with the technical expertise, personnel, and equipment necessary to perform electrical, life-safety, and fire-protection system modifications within the Powerhouse Gate Repair Pit at The Dalles Lock and Dam. The Gate Repair Pit is currently classified as a space that is not normally occupied. This requirement will modify the area to support its classification as a normally occupied space by correcting identified deficiencies in the existing fire-protection and life-safety systems and bringing the facility into compliance with applicable fire and safety codes. Project Scope. The work consists of three primary areas: electrical, life-safety, and fire-protection improvements. Incidental and supporting work is anticipated to include concrete penetrations; conduit, cable, and piping removal and installation; demolition and replacement or modification of wall-mounted electrical panels and doors; and integration of new fire-protection components with the Powerhouse�s existing fire-detection system. Electrical work includes general electrical repairs and modifications, including relocation of terminal boxes; rewiring of the welder control panel; modification of electrical enclosures and wall plates; relocation and modification of existing welding receptacles, including associated cable installation and minor cover-plate fabrication; and evaluation, replacement, rewiring, and reconfiguration of the blower electrical switch. The life-safety work includes furnishing and installing fire extinguishers, eyewash stations, gas-cylinder storage-limit markings, floor-level identification markings, and retractable doorway caution barriers, necessary to achieve compliance with applicable OSHA and NFPA requirements. The work also includes furnishing and installing protective plates for the existing oxygen and acetylene cylinders. The fire-protection work includes removal of the existing Gate Repair Pit entry door and installation of NFPA-rated fire doors; installation of siren/strobe notification appliances; repair, replacement, or reinforcement of firestopping at wall penetrations; and installation of fiber-optic heat-detection systems along the interior walls of the pit. The work also includes programming and integrating the fire-detection system to initiate damper closure and blower-motor shutdown upon fire detection, including all required cable, conduit, relays, controls, and associated devices. Project Location. The construction work will be performed at the Dalles Lock and Dam near The Dalles, Oregon, in Klickitat County Washington. Contractor access to the work site is on the Oregon side of the Columbia River from exit 88 on I-84. Project Purpose. The purpose of this project is to correct identified life-safety and fire-protection deficiencies within the Powerhouse Gate Repair Pit at The Dalles Lock and Dam, allowing the space to be safely classified and operated as normally occupied and bringing the facility into compliance with applicable OSHA, NFPA, fire, and life-safety requirements. Project Objectives. Construct the required electrical, life-safety, and fire-protection improvements in accordance with the contract documents and applicable codes. Test, integrate, and commission the completed systems to verify safe and reliable operation. Complete the work safely and within the established project schedule while minimizing impacts to Powerhouse operations. NAICS. Monday, September 28 & Tuesday, September 29, 2026 ? 9:00 a.m. � 3:00 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) ? Virtual Event | Microsoft Teams ?? FREE to Participate ? Space is limited. Registration will close once all vendor presentation slots have been filled. The Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS), Division of Contracts and Grants Management (DCGM), invites Native American-owned small businesses to participate in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, a two-day virtual event dedicated to strengthening partnerships, expanding the Albuquerque Area IHS supplier base, and increasing awareness of the capabilities of Native American-owned businesses. Held shortly before Indigenous Peoples� Day, this event provides Native American-owned small businesses, including eligible Small Business Indian Firms (SBIFs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), an opportunity to introduce their organizations and showcase their capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals, program stakeholders, and organizational leadership. ?? Event Overview Day One will begin with introductions from Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals and a brief overview of the Buy Indian Act and its role in supporting Indian economic enterprises through federal procurement. Following the opening session, participating vendors will receive an individually scheduled 10-minute presentation slot to introduce their businesses and highlight their capabilities, qualifications, products, services, past performance, and other information relevant to potential Albuquerque Area IHS requirements. Vendor capability presentations will continue throughout both days. ? Vendor Capability Presentations This is your opportunity to show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals. Vendors are encouraged to use their presentation time to highlight information such as: Core capabilities and areas of expertise Products and/or services offered Relevant experience and past performance Geographic areas served Unique capabilities or solutions How your business can support IHS healthcare operations and mission requirements ? Who Will Be in the Audience? The Industry Day is designed to connect Native American-owned businesses with Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals involved in identifying requirements, conducting market research, planning acquisitions, making purchases, and administering contracts. The audience may include: Buyers Contract Specialists Contracting Officers Contracting Officer�s Representatives (CORs) Government Purchase Cardholders and Approving Officials Service Unit Chief Executive Officers Program and technical personnel Albuquerque Area leadership This broad audience provides participating businesses an opportunity to increase awareness of their capabilities across IHS while helping acquisition and program personnel identify potential sources for future requirements. ? Why Participate? The Albuquerque Area IHS is committed to meaningful industry engagement and expanding opportunities for Native American-owned small businesses. Participation in Industry Day provides businesses an opportunity to: Introduce their company directly to IHS acquisition, program, and organizational personnel Increase awareness of their products, services, and capabilities Help IHS identify new and emerging industry capabilities Support IHS market research and acquisition planning Develop relationships with acquisition and program personnel Increase awareness of potential opportunities to do business with IHS At the same time, these interactions help Albuquerque Area IHS broaden its procurement base, identify qualified sources, increase competition, and strengthen relationships with the Native American-owned business community. We want to learn what your business can do for IHS. ? How to Participate Native American-owned small businesses interested in participating should email: ALBAreaSmallBusiness@ihs.gov Please indicate your interest in participating in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day and include your business name and primary point of contact. Upon receipt of your email, the Albuquerque Area IHS will provide a registration form to collect additional business information and assist with scheduling. Presentation times will be scheduled in advance. Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities, qualifications, products, and/or services. Space is limited, and registration will close once all available vendor presentation slots have been filled. Vendors are encouraged to register early. Additional event and Microsoft Teams information will be provided to registered participants prior to the event. ? Building Partnerships in Support of the IHS Mission Through the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, DCGM seeks to strengthen relationships with Native American-owned businesses, expand awareness of industry capabilities, broaden the Albuquerque Area procurement base, and identify qualified sources capable of supporting healthcare delivery. These partnerships help ensure that Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals have access to capable and innovative businesses that can provide the supplies, services, equipment, and solutions necessary to support direct patient care and advance the IHS mission: �To raise the physical, mental, social and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level.� ? Join us September 28-29, 2026, and show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! ?? Important Notice This Industry Day is being conducted for informational, outreach, and market research purposes. This event is not a bidder�s conference, solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quote, promise to contract, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Participation in this event does not guarantee consideration for or award of any future procurement. The Government will not assume liability for costs incurred by any participant associated with attending the event or preparing, submitting, or presenting information, capability statements, presentations, or other materials. Costs incurred in response to this notice will not be considered allowable direct or indirect charges to the Government.
